title: Require deploy-role authorization for release execution
action: Repair the incomplete first-round commit. First add behavior tests that fail for missing or mismatched issuer session, runtime mismatch, unknown or wrong feature, missing or wrong approved plan, wrong stage, wrong role, wrong version, wrong commit, stale or malformed expiry, replay, and authorization-marker storage failure. Then enforce the approved Release authorization protocol: bind and validate session, feature, runtime, plan, deployment stage, deploy role, exact version, main commit, and two-hour lifetime; create a durable one-use marker only after every check passes; keep all prior release safety checks unchanged. Amend the existing slr-6 commit instead of adding a commit.
verify: PATH="${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin:$PATH" cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml deploy && bash -n scripts/release.sh

truths: A direct release script call refuses before mutation.
Only an unconsumed deployment dispatch under deploy authorizes its exact issuer session, feature, runtime, version, approved plan, and main commit.
Stale, malformed-expiry, replayed, forged, wrong-session, wrong-feature, wrong-runtime, wrong-plan, wrong-stage, wrong-role, wrong-version, wrong-commit, and marker-storage failures refuse.
Tests directly exercise every named refusal before cap.
Existing release safety checks remain unchanged after authorization.

acceptance: Approved releases cannot bypass the deploy role, while scripts/release.sh remains the implementation.
